chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin and Abu Ayyub and Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him, 'What do you say regarding a woman who died and left her husband, and her brothers from her mother, and brothers and sisters from her father?' He said: 'For the husband is the half, being three shares, and for her brothers from her mother is the one-third, being two shares, male and female being equal in it, and the one remaining share, so it is for the brothers and sisters from the father, for the male is like the portion of two females, because the shares do not increase (deficiency), and that the husband is not reduced from the half, nor the brothers from the mother, from their third, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: "But if they are more than that, they shall be sharers in the third." And if there was one, so for him is the one-sixth.'

And what Allah means by His Elevated Words, 'And if a man is inherited by a Kalala or a woman, and for him is a brother or a sister, so for each one from them is the one-sixth,' is that He means by that the brothers and sisters from the mother in particular.

They ask you for a verdict. Say: Allah gives you a verdict concerning the Kalala. If a person died and there is no child for him, and for him is a sister, meaning a sister from a father and a mother, or a sister from a father, so for her is half of what he left, and he inherits her if there is no child for her.

So if there are two, so for the two of them is two-thirds from what he left, and if there were brethren, men and women, so for the male is like the portion of two females. And they are the ones who are increased and decreased.

He said: 'And if a woman left her husband, and her two sisters from her mother, and her two sisters from her father, for the husband is the half, being three shares, and for her two sisters from her mother is the one-third, being two shares, and for her two sisters from her father is the one-sixth, being one share. And if she was only one, so it is for her, because the two sisters from the father do not increase over what remains. And if there was a brother from the father, he would not increase over what remains.'

key_terms.إِخْوَةٌ وَ أَخَوَاتٌ لِأَبِيهَا: Brothers and sisters from the father (paternal siblings)
key_terms.الْكَلالَة: Kalala (one who has no direct ascendants or descendants)
key_terms.لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ: For the male is the portion of two females

ai.seo_question: How is the estate distributed when a woman leaves a husband, maternal siblings, and paternal siblings?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the specific mechanics of fractional inheritance (Fara'id) when multiple sibling groups compete for the residual estate, emphasizing the Shia principle that 'shares do not increase' (la ta'ul al-awsad) to preserve the fixed portions of the husband and maternal siblings. It provides a critical exegetical link between Quranic verses on 'Kalala' (4:12, 4:176) and the practical application of inheritance rules for half-siblings, distinguishing between maternal and paternal shares based on the presence of a spouse. The narration underscores the scholarly tradition of deriving detailed legal rulings directly from the Imams' interpretation of Quranic terminology, particularly regarding the equality of males and females in maternal inheritance versus the double-share rule for paternal siblings.
